title: Signal naming style
description: Keep signal names in one recognizable style.

title: Low-active suffix
description: Low-active signal names should use the _n suffix.

title: Multiplexer signal naming
description: Multiplexer signal names should reveal width or input count.

title: Magic number
description: Replace unexplained numeric literals with a localparam, parameter, or macro.

title: Multiple always drivers
description: Avoid assigning one signal in multiple always blocks.

title: Combinational sensitivity
description: Combinational logic should use always @(*) or assign.

title: Combinational blocking assignment
description: Combinational always blocks should use blocking assignments.

title: Combinational completeness
description: Combinational branches and case statements should assign every output path.

title: Sequential posedge
description: Sequential logic should use always @(posedge clock).

title: Sequential nonblocking assignment
description: Sequential always blocks should use nonblocking assignments.

title: Negedge trigger
description: Avoid negedge-triggered logic unless a protocol requires it.

title: Edge signal kind
description: Edge-triggered sensitivity signals should be clocks or resets.

title: Clock used as data
description: Clock signals should not be used as ordinary data inside sequential logic.

title: Synchronous reset preference
description: Prefer synchronous reset when async reset appears in sensitivity lists.

title: Internal inout port
description: Internal modules should avoid inout ports.

title: Instance port formatting
description: Instances should use named, multiline, one-port-per-line mapping.

title: Explicit signal width
description: Declare explicit widths for non-parameter signals.

title: Declaration initializer
description: Avoid declaration initializers for registers in synthesizable modules.

title: Initial block
description: Avoid initial blocks in synthesizable design modules.

title: Expensive arithmetic operator
description: Avoid multiply, divide, and modulo operators unless hardware cost is intentional.
